accepted.question_text: In a two-queue polling system with cyclic service, where arrivals to both queues are independent Poisson processes, service times and switch-over times are independent, and the first queue uses gated service while the second queue uses 1-limited service, determine the joint probability generating function of the steady-state queue-length vector at polling instants. Equivalently, determine the joint queue-length PGFs F1(z1, z2) and F2(z1, z2) for this G/1-L polling system.

evidence.quote: Open problem 1. Determine the joint queue-length PGF at polling instants in the two-queue G/1-L polling system.
In this section we restrict ourselves to the case of N = 2 queues. We are interested in determining F1(z1, z2) and F2(z1, z2).

accepted.question_text: Consider a cyclic polling system with a fixed cyclic order of N queues and general renewal arrival processes at the queues. When the switch-over times are deterministic and all deterministic switch-over times grow without bound while their ratios remain fixed, provide a rigorous proof that the system converges to a deterministic cyclic system.
accepted.context_brief: Renewal arrivals with large deterministic switch-overs

evidence.quote: Open problem 2. Provide a rigourous proof of Conjecture 4.2, which states that a cyclic polling system with general (renewal) arrival processes converges to a deterministic cyclic system when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity.
Conjecture 4.2. A cyclic polling system with general (renewal) arrival processes converges to a deterministic cyclic system when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity.

accepted.question_text: Classify which polling systems, in terms of their service disciplines, visit disciplines, and scheduling disciplines, have the following asymptotic property: as switch-over times become large, the system exhibits the same deterministic limiting behaviour discussed in the paper, including in settings with dynamic visit orders rather than a fixed pre-determined queue order.

evidence.quote: A resulting open problem is, therefore, the classification of polling systems in terms of service, visit and scheduling disciplines, which exhibit the discussed behaviour.

That is, [14] shows via numerical testing that similar limit theorems as presented here carry over to systems with Poisson arrivals and dynamic visit orders (i.e., there exists no pre-determined order in which the queues are served).
